Blocks.Section: Verified on LinkedIn - FAQ
Blocks.Text: This comprehensive FAQ provides answers to common questions about integrating and using the Verified on LinkedIn API, including access, authentication, data returned, policy guidelines, and developer support.

Blocks.Section: What is the Verified on LinkedIn API?
SectionPath: What is the Verified on LinkedIn API?
Blocks.Text: The Verified on LinkedIn API enables you to retrieve LinkedIn members' verified identity and workplace information after they grant explicit consent through OAuth 2.0. You can display the "Verified on LinkedIn" badge within your app to build trust and authenticity into your platform.

Blocks.Section: What is the Verified on LinkedIn API?
SectionPath: What is the Verified on LinkedIn API?
Blocks.Text: More than 80 million LinkedIn members have confirmed their identity with a government-issued ID or verified their workplace using a company email. Read more about LinkedIn verifications.

Blocks.Section: What are the different tiers?
Blocks.Text: LinkedIn offers three tiers of the Verified on LinkedIn API:

Blocks.Section: What are the different tiers?
What are the different tiers?
Blocks.Text: See Overview for detailed tier comparison.

Blocks.Section: How do I choose which tier to use?
SectionPath: How do I choose which tier to use?
Blocks.Text:
Development: Start here to test the API with your admin account. Perfect for prototyping and learning.
Lite: Ready for production with basic verification data. No cost, suitable for SMBs and startups.
Plus: Enterprise-grade with detailed verification metadata, organization details, and bulk validation API. Requires business partnership.

Blocks.Section: What data does each tier return?
SectionPath: What data does each tier return?
Blocks.Text:
All Tiers: Completed verification categories (IDENTITY, WORKPLACE), and a verificationUrl for members eligible to complete missing verifications.
Plus Tier Only: Organization names, verification methods, verification timestamps, education data, and basic profile details.

Blocks.Section: What data does each tier return?
SectionPath: What data does each tier return?
Blocks.Text: Note

Blocks.Section: What data does each tier return?
SectionPath: What data does each tier return?
Blocks.Text: For extended metadata (organization details, verification methods, timestamps), use Verified on LinkedIn Plus. See Overview for tier comparison.

Blocks.Section: What Member consent is required?
Blocks.Text: Members must explicitly grant consent via LinkedIn's OAuth 2.0 authorization flow before your app can access their verification data. Without consent, no data can be retrieved. Consent is required once unless you add new scopes.

Blocks.Section: Does the API share unverified or pending data?
SectionPath: Does the API share unverified or pending data?
Blocks.Text: No. The API only returns completed verification categories. Members who are not yet verified will receive a verificationUrl to complete the process on LinkedIn.

Blocks.Section: Can Members revoke access?
Blocks.Text: Yes. Members can revoke access anytime from their LinkedIn account settings at https://www.linkedin.com/mypreferences/d/data-sharing-for-permitted-services. After revocation, all subsequent API requests return 401 Unauthorized until the member re-consents.

Blocks.Section: Which OAuth scopes are required?
Blocks.Text: Development & Lite Tiers:

Blocks.Section: Which OAuth scopes are required?
Blocks.Text:
r_profile_basicinfo – Basic profile information (name, email, profile URL, picture)
r_verify – Verification categories only

Blocks.Section: Which OAuth scopes are required?
Blocks.Text: Plus Tier:

Blocks.Section: Which OAuth scopes are required?
Blocks.Text:
r_verify_details – Detailed verification status and metadata
r_profile_basicinfo – Basic profile information
r_most_recent_education – Most recent education details
r_primary_current_experience – Current workplace information

Blocks.Section: Which OAuth scopes are required?
Blocks.Text: Important

Blocks.Section: Which OAuth scopes are required?
Blocks.Text: Key Difference: r_verify returns only verification categories (e.g., ["IDENTITY", "WORKPLACE"]), while r_verify_details returns full metadata including verified names, timestamps, methods, and organization details.

Blocks.Section: How do I obtain access tokens?
SectionPath: How do I obtain access tokens?
Blocks.Text: Use the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow to exchange an authorization code for an access token and refresh token.

Blocks.Section: How do I obtain access tokens?
SectionPath: How do I obtain access tokens?
Blocks.Text: Token Characteristics:

Blocks.Section: How do I obtain access tokens?
SectionPath: How do I obtain access tokens?
Blocks.Text:
Access tokens are valid for 60 days
Refresh tokens remain valid for 1 year and can be used to obtain new access tokens without requiring member re-consent
Member consent is required once (unless you add new scopes)

Blocks.Section: How do I obtain access tokens?
SectionPath: How do I obtain access tokens?
Blocks.Text: For detailed implementation, see Authorization Code Flow Guide.

Blocks.Section: Should I request all scopes at once?
SectionPath: Should I request all scopes at once?
Blocks.Text: Yes. Request all required scopes in a single authorization request to provide the best user experience and avoid multiple authorization prompts. This gives you:

Blocks.Section: Should I request all scopes at once?
SectionPath: Should I request all scopes at once?
Blocks.Text:
✅ Single consent flow - Member authorizes once instead of multiple times
✅ Complete data access - Get all profile and verification data in one session
✅ Better UX - Avoid interrupting member with additional authorization requests
✅ Simplified implementation - No need to manage partial authorization states

Blocks.Section: What happens when my access token expires?
SectionPath: What happens when my access token expires?
Blocks.Text: When an access token expires, API calls return 401 Unauthorized. Use your refresh token to obtain a new access token without requiring the member to re-authorize. If the refresh token has also expired (after 1 year), the member must complete the OAuth flow again.

Blocks.Section: What happens when my access token expires?
SectionPath: What happens when my access token expires?
Blocks.Text: See Authentication Guide for implementation details.

Blocks.Section: Do tokens work across tier upgrades?
SectionPath: Do tokens work across tier upgrades?
Blocks.Text: Yes! When you upgrade from Development to Lite or Lite to Plus:

Blocks.Section: Do tokens work across tier upgrades?
SectionPath: Do tokens work across tier upgrades?
Blocks.Text:
Existing access tokens remain valid
Members don't need to re-authorize (unless you add new scopes)
Only request new consent if adding scopes

Blocks.Section: How do I add more scopes?
SectionPath: How do I add more scopes?
Blocks.Text: If you need additional OAuth scopes (e.g., upgrading to Plus tier):

Blocks.Section: How do I add more scopes?
SectionPath: How do I add more scopes?
Blocks.Text:
Update your authorization URL with new scopes
Ask member to re-authorize
New tokens will include additional scopes

What endpoints should I use?

SectionPath: What is the correct API request format?

Blocks.Section: What is the correct API request format?
SectionPath: What is the correct API request format?

Blocks.Section: What should I do if the API returns a verificationUrl?
SectionPath: What should I do if the API returns a verificationUrl?
Blocks.Text: Display a "Verify on LinkedIn" button and redirect the member to the returned URL. After the member completes verification on LinkedIn, call /verificationReport again to refresh the updated verification categories.

Blocks.Section: What should I do if the API returns a verificationUrl?
SectionPath: What should I do if the API returns a verificationUrl?
Blocks.Text: Always re-query /verificationReport to obtain a fresh verificationUrl instead of reusing older links, as they may expire.

Blocks.Section: How can I require members to periodically re-verify?
SectionPath: How can I require members to periodically re-verify?
Blocks.Text: Use the optional verifiedWithinDays query parameter when calling /verificationReport.

Blocks.Section: How can I require members to periodically re-verify?
SectionPath: How can I require members to periodically re-verify?
Blocks.Text: For example:

Blocks.Section: How can I require members to periodically re-verify?
SectionPath: How can I require members to periodically re-verify?
Blocks.Text: GET /verificationReport?verifiedWithinDays=365

Blocks.Section: How can I require members to periodically re-verify?
SectionPath: How can I require members to periodically re-verify?
Blocks.Text: If an existing verification is older than the requested freshness window and the member is still eligible to re-verify the existing verification, the response includes a verificationUrl so the member can re-verify.

Blocks.Section: How can I require members to periodically re-verify?
SectionPath: How can I require members to periodically re-verify?
Blocks.Text:
Existing verification data continues to be returned and is not removed or invalidated.
The verifiedWithinDays parameter only affects whether a verificationUrl is returned.
No verification data is removed or invalidated.
If the existing verification satisfies the requested freshness window, no re-verification is requested.

Blocks.Section: How can I require members to periodically re-verify?
SectionPath: How can I require members to periodically re-verify?
Blocks.Text: See the /verificationReport API for complete details.

Blocks.Section: Does Verified on LinkedIn support OAuth state?
SectionPath: Does Verified on LinkedIn support OAuth state?
Blocks.Text: Yes. The state parameter is the only supported dynamic query parameter in redirect URLs. It is excluded from redirect URL validation and preserved in the final redirect URL after verification. Partners can use state for CSRF protection, session continuity, and request tracking.

Blocks.Section: Can I store verification results?
Blocks.Text: You may cache verification results temporarily for performance optimization, but you must:

Blocks.Section: Can I store verification results?
Blocks.Text:
Refresh them periodically to ensure accuracy
Comply with LinkedIn's API Terms
Not store verification data indefinitely

Blocks.Section: Can I store verification results?
Blocks.Text: For Plus tier, see Data Freshness Guide for best practices on keeping member data up-to-date.

Blocks.Section: Can I show badges for all users?
SectionPath: Can I show badges for all users?
Blocks.Text: Only display the "Verified on LinkedIn" badge for users who have completed one or more verification categories, as indicated by the API response. Follow the Branding & UX Guidelines for correct badge usage.

Blocks.Section: What are the rate limits?
What are the rate limits?
Blocks.Text: If you exceed these limits, the API returns a 429 Too Many Requests response.

Blocks.Section: What timeout should I use?
Blocks.Text:
Standard endpoints (/identityMe, /verificationReport): 5 seconds
Bulk validation (/validationStatus): 30 seconds

Blocks.Section: How do I handle missing optional fields?
SectionPath: How do I handle missing optional fields?
Blocks.Text: Some fields may be missing from API responses (e.g., email address, profile picture). Your implementation should:

Blocks.Section: How do I handle missing optional fields?
SectionPath: How do I handle missing optional fields?
Blocks.Text:
✅ Handle missing optional fields gracefully
✅ Display fallback content when data is unavailable
✅ Log missing fields for debugging

Blocks.Section: How do I validate member ID uniqueness?
SectionPath: How do I validate member ID uniqueness?
Blocks.Text: This is critical for security. You must validate that each id is unique in your system to prevent a single LinkedIn account from verifying multiple accounts on your platform.

Blocks.Section: How do I validate member ID uniqueness?
SectionPath: How do I validate member ID uniqueness?
Blocks.Text: Best Practices:

Blocks.Section: How do I validate member ID uniqueness?
SectionPath: How do I validate member ID uniqueness?
Blocks.Text:
✅ Enforce uniqueness at the database level (UNIQUE constraint)
✅ Check for existing LinkedIn ID before saving new verification
✅ Log security alerts when duplicate attempts are detected
✅ Display clear error messages to members
✅ Provide support contact for legitimate edge cases

Blocks.Section: How do I validate member ID uniqueness?
SectionPath: How do I validate member ID uniqueness?
Blocks.Text: Note

Blocks.Section: How do I validate member ID uniqueness?
SectionPath: How do I validate member ID uniqueness?
Blocks.Text: Always use the id field (available since version 202510). The userId field will be deprecated in future versions and should only be used for temporary backward compatibility during migration from older API versions.

Blocks.Section: How do I keep member data up-to-date?
SectionPath: How do I keep member data up-to-date?
Blocks.Text: Plus tier only. You have two options:

Blocks.Section: How do I keep member data up-to-date?
SectionPath: How do I keep member data up-to-date?
Blocks.Text:
Polling with /validationStatus – Call the bulk validation API daily to check if member data has changed
Push Notifications – Receive real-time webhooks when member data changes

Blocks.Section: How do I keep member data up-to-date?
SectionPath: How do I keep member data up-to-date?
Blocks.Text: See Data Freshness Guide for detailed implementation strategies.

Blocks.Section: What is the /validationStatus API?
Blocks.Text: The /validationStatus API (Plus tier only) allows you to bulk-check up to 500 members at once to see if their verification or profile data has changed. It returns status values:

Blocks.Section: What is the /validationStatus API?
Blocks.Text:
VALID – Data is current, no action needed
INVALID – Data should be refreshed by calling /verificationReport and /identityMe
VALID_WITH_UPDATES – Data is valid but member re-verified (optional refresh)

Blocks.Section: What is the /validationStatus API?
Blocks.Text: This reduces unnecessary API calls compared to polling individual members.

Blocks.Section: How do push notifications work?
Blocks.Text: Push notifications provide real-time updates when member data changes. To use them:

Blocks.Section: How do push notifications work?
Blocks.Text:
Contact LinkedIn API Support to set up webhooks for your application
Receive FEDERATED_MEMBER_DATA_STATUS_CHANGE events when member data changes
Refresh data by calling /verificationReport and /identityMe with the member's access token

Blocks.Section: How do push notifications work?
Blocks.Text: Important

Blocks.Section: How do push notifications work?
Blocks.Text: Push notifications indicate that changes exist—they do not contain the actual updated data. You must call the actual endpoints to retrieve the new data.

Blocks.Section: What should I do when I receive a push notification?
SectionPath: What should I do when I receive a push notification?
Blocks.Text:
Check if isAccessRevoked is true:

If yes → Remove the member's data from your system
If no → Continue to step 2


Check the status fields in the notification:

INVALID → Must refresh data by calling /verificationReport and/or /identityMe
VALID_WITH_UPDATES → Optionally refresh to get latest data
VALID → No action needed


Call the appropriate endpoints with the member's access token
Update your stored data

Blocks.Section: What fields should I persist for data freshness?
SectionPath: What fields should I persist for data freshness?
Blocks.Text: To implement data freshness strategies, you must store:

Blocks.Section: What fields should I persist for data freshness?
SectionPath: What fields should I persist for data freshness?

Rows.Text: Required for /validationStatus checks and push notifications
Needed to obtain new access tokens without member re-authorization
Timestamp to ignore stale notifications and avoid unnecessary API calls

Blocks.Section: How do I implement polling with /validationStatus?
SectionPath: How do I implement polling with /validationStatus?
Blocks.Text: Polling involves two steps:

Blocks.Section: How do I implement polling with /validationStatus?
SectionPath: How do I implement polling with /validationStatus?
Blocks.Text: Step 1: Check Status (2-legged OAuth, no member consent needed)

Blocks.Section: How do I implement polling with /validationStatus?
SectionPath: How do I implement polling with /validationStatus?
Blocks.Text:
Call /validationStatus with up to 500 member ids in a single request
Receive status for each member: VALID, INVALID, or VALID_WITH_UPDATES

Blocks.Section: How do I implement polling with /validationStatus?
SectionPath: How do I implement polling with /validationStatus?
Blocks.Text: Step 2: Refresh Data (3-legged OAuth, member consent required)

Blocks.Section: How do I implement polling with /validationStatus?
SectionPath: How do I implement polling with /validationStatus?
Blocks.Text:
For members with INVALID or VALID_WITH_UPDATES status only
Call /verificationReport and /identityMe with the member's access token
Store the updated data

Blocks.Section: How do I implement polling with /validationStatus?
SectionPath: How do I implement polling with /validationStatus?
Blocks.Text: This two-step approach minimizes API calls by only refreshing data for members who have changes.

Blocks.Section: How often should I poll for data changes?
SectionPath: How often should I poll for data changes?
Blocks.Text: Recommended: Once per day during off-peak hours.

Blocks.Section: How often should I poll for data changes?
SectionPath: How often should I poll for data changes?
Blocks.Text: Best Practices:

Blocks.Section: How often should I poll for data changes?
SectionPath: How often should I poll for data changes?
Blocks.Text:
✅ Run polling during off-peak hours to minimize impact
✅ Batch requests (up to 500 members per call) to stay within rate limits
✅ Only call actual endpoints for members with VALID_WITH_UPDATES or INVALID status
✅ Implement exponential backoff for rate limit errors
✅ Store critical fields (id, refresh_token, lastRefreshedAt) before implementing polling

Blocks.Section: Is data freshness available for all tiers?
SectionPath: Is data freshness available for all tiers?
Blocks.Text: No. Data freshness strategies (polling and push notifications) are Plus tier only. Development and Lite tiers do not have access to /validationStatus or push notifications.

Blocks.Section: How should I store OAuth tokens?
SectionPath: How should I store OAuth tokens?
Blocks.Text: This is critical for security. You must securely store OAuth access tokens and refresh tokens with encryption.

Blocks.Section: How should I store OAuth tokens?
SectionPath: How should I store OAuth tokens?
Blocks.Text: Best Practices:

Blocks.Section: How should I store OAuth tokens?
SectionPath: How should I store OAuth tokens?
Blocks.Text:
✅ Encrypt tokens using AES-256-GCM or equivalent
✅ Store in secure backend database with proper access controls
✅ Implement token rotation and secure deletion policies
✅ Never store tokens in client-side storage (cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage)
✅ Log access to tokens for audit purposes

Blocks.Section: Why do I need to store refresh tokens?
SectionPath: Why do I need to store refresh tokens?
Blocks.Text: Storing refresh tokens is necessary to generate new access tokens when needed to refresh member data without requiring the member to re-authorize. This enables you to keep member profile and verification information up-to-date through background processes.

Blocks.Section: What are the general security best practices?
SectionPath: What are the general security best practices?
Blocks.Text:
✅ Store tokens securely – Encrypt at rest, never expose in client-side code
✅ Use refresh tokens – Don't make users re-authenticate every 60 days
✅ Request minimum scopes – Only request what you need
✅ Handle token expiry gracefully – Implement automatic refresh logic
✅ Validate redirect URIs – Must match exactly with Developer Portal settings
✅ Implement CSRF protection – Use state parameter in OAuth flow
✅ Use HTTPS only for all API calls

Blocks.Section: What are the approved use cases?
SectionPath: What are the approved use cases?
Blocks.Text: The API is designed for trust enhancement, not regulatory compliance or eligibility decisions. Approved use cases include:

Blocks.Section: What are the approved use cases?
SectionPath: What are the approved use cases?

Rows.Text: Professional communities, networking platforms, online marketplaces, peer-to-peer exchanges
Event registration, professional conferences, community moderation, alumni groups
Buyer/seller verification, freelance platforms, service-sharing, resale platforms

Blocks.Section: What are the restricted use cases?
SectionPath: What are the restricted use cases?
Blocks.Text: The API cannot be used for:

Blocks.Section: What are the restricted use cases?
SectionPath: What are the restricted use cases?

Rows.Text: Not an employment screening tool. Do not use to rank or approve candidates.
Does not include criminal, financial, or government background data.
Not related to creditworthiness or insurability.
Cannot be used for rental or housing determinations.
Not a substitute for official ID verification systems.
Should complement — not replace your platform's trust and risk systems.

Blocks.Section: Can I use this API for background checks or credit decisions?
SectionPath: Can I use this API for background checks or credit decisions?
Blocks.Text: No. The API cannot be used for employment eligibility, credit scoring, housing, or any similar decision-making purposes.

Blocks.Section: Can I aggregate or resell LinkedIn verification data?
SectionPath: Can I aggregate or resell LinkedIn verification data?
Blocks.Text: No. You may only use verification data within your own app for the member who granted consent. Aggregation, resale, or redistribution is strictly prohibited.

Blocks.Section: Is there a review process?
Blocks.Text: Yes. Verified on LinkedIn applications undergo automated and manual reviews. LinkedIn may request clarifications or revoke access for policy violations.

Blocks.Section: How should I display the "Verify on LinkedIn" button?
SectionPath: How should I display the "Verify on LinkedIn" button?
Blocks.Text:
Purpose: Routes members to LinkedIn to complete identity or workplace verification
Placement: Display in contexts where verification is required
State: Render only when the API response includes a valid verificationUrl
Label: Button text must remain "Verify on LinkedIn". No modifications such as "LinkedIn Verify" or "Verify via LinkedIn"
Do not cache: Always use the latest verificationUrl from each API response

SectionPath: How should I display the "Verify on LinkedIn" button?

Blocks.Section: What do I do if I get a 401 Unauthorized error?
SectionPath: What do I do if I get a 401 Unauthorized error?
Blocks.Text: This typically means:

Blocks.Section: What do I do if I get a 401 Unauthorized error?
SectionPath: What do I do if I get a 401 Unauthorized error?
Blocks.Text:
Your access token has expired – Use your refresh token to get a new one
Your refresh token has expired – Ask the member to re-authorize
The member revoked access – Ask them to re-authorize from your app

Blocks.Section: What do I do if I get a 403 Forbidden error?
SectionPath: What do I do if I get a 403 Forbidden error?
Blocks.Text: Ensure your access token includes the required scopes:

SectionPath: What do I do if I get a 429 Too Many Requests error?
Blocks.Text: You've exceeded rate limits. Check:

Blocks.Section: What do I do if I get a 429 Too Many Requests error?
SectionPath: What do I do if I get a 429 Too Many Requests error?
Blocks.Text:
Per Application: 5,000 requests per day
Per member: 500 requests per day

Blocks.Section: What do I do if I get a 429 Too Many Requests error?
SectionPath: What do I do if I get a 429 Too Many Requests error?
Blocks.Text: Implement request throttling and caching to reduce API calls.

Blocks.Section: My redirect URI isn't working. What should I check?
SectionPath: My redirect URI isn't working. What should I check?
Blocks.Text: Ensure your redirect URI exactly matches the one configured in your app settings in the Developer Portal. The match is case-sensitive and must include the protocol (http/https).

Blocks.Section: The verificationUrl returned is expired or invalid. What should I do?
SectionPath: The verificationUrl returned is expired or invalid. What should I do?
Blocks.Text: Always re-query /verificationReport to obtain a fresh verificationUrl instead of reusing older links. URLs expire after a period of time.

Blocks.Section: How long does verification remain valid?
SectionPath: How long does verification remain valid?
Blocks.Text: Verification categories reflect LinkedIn's current record for the member. If the member updates or removes their verification, the API response will reflect the change accordingly. This is why you should refresh verification data periodically.
